articles.title: Greater L.A. Office Leasing Shows Signs of Life — Finally
articles.narrative: Greater Los Angeles' office market is showing signs of recovery, with nearly 4 million square feet of office space leased in the second quarter, a 15% increase from the previous quarter and 8% year-over-year. This quarterly total is 22% above the five-year average, approaching 2019 levels. However, the recovery is primarily driven by renewals and expansions rather than new demand, and overall availability remains high at 26.6%. Sublease availability has declined for seven consecutive quarters, falling to 6.7 million square feet in Q2.
articles.market_intelligence: Landlords are still offering concession packages near historic highs to attract tenants, which keeps net effective rents below quoted rates. Distressed assets transitioning to new ownership, such as Capital Group's $210 million acquisition of Bank of America Plaza, are expected to help accelerate leasing activity.

articles.title: Zar Property NY Buys 118 West 22nd Street for $28M
articles.narrative: Zar Property NY has acquired 118 West 22nd Street, a 12-story mixed-use building in Manhattan's Flatiron District, for $28 million. The seller was Adlie Associates, which had owned the property since 1986. The acquisition was supported by a $19.6 million financing package arranged by Filler Capital and provided by J.P. Morgan, marking a significant transaction for the buyer.

data_points.address: 118 West 22nd Street, New York City, NY
data_points.notable_features: Designed by architect Frederick Zobel, who also designed several structures protected by the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission.

articles.title: Obra Supplies $31M Refi on Arizona Northrop Grumman-Leased Office Property
articles.narrative: Silver Creek Development has secured $31.4 million in bridge debt from Obra Real Estate to refinance a single-tenant office complex in Gilbert, AZ. The 2021-built property is fully leased to a global aerospace and defense technology company, reflecting continued demand for high-quality assets with institutional-grade tenancy and experienced sponsorship. Arrow Real Estate Advisors arranged the transaction, which closed in under 30 days.

data_points.notable_features: Located within the 63-acre Gilbert Spectrum Business Park, 20 miles southeast of Downtown Phoenix.
data_points.project_notes: Silver Creek acquired the property for $43.1 million in early 2021.

articles.title: Manhattan’s Office Leasing Reaches Velocity Not Seen Since 2002: Report
articles.narrative: Manhattan's office leasing activity in the first half of 2026 reached levels not seen since 2002, with nearly 23 million square feet leased, indicating a strong market recovery. Demand outpaced tightening supply, leading to a sharp increase in average asking rents, which rose 5.7 percent annually to $78.03 per square foot. Law firms and technology companies were major drivers of this activity, with professional services accounting for 30 percent of the quarter's leasing and AI-related leases surpassing the total for 2025.

people.name: Franklin Wallach
people.title: Executive Managing Director for Research and Business

articles.market_intelligence: Manhattan's office market is experiencing a significant recovery, with leasing velocity in the first half of 2026 being the strongest since 2002. Average asking rents increased by 5.7% annually, the sharpest midyear growth since 2016. The overall availability rate contracted to 13%, and sublease supply has dipped below pre-pandemic levels. Hudson Yards remains the priciest submarket, with average asking rents of $153 per square foot.

articles.title: Miami’s Office Leasing Jumps Nearly 45% in Q2
articles.narrative: Miami-Dade County's office market experienced a significant surge in leasing activity during Q2 2026, with a nearly 45% year-over-year increase, pushing average asking rents to a record high of $67.12 per square foot. This robust demand, driven by an influx of family offices, financial firms, and technology companies, has led to a tightening vacancy rate, which fell to 14.9%. Class A buildings, particularly new, amenity-rich properties, saw rents climb 6% year-over-year to $80.85 per square foot, reflecting strong competition for premium space.

articles.title: Northmarq Secures $13.7M Bridge Loan for Innerbelt Business Center in Metro St. Louis
articles.narrative: Northmarq has secured a $13.7 million bridge loan for Fountain Real Estate Capital to finance the acquisition of Innerbelt Business Center, a 191,925-square-foot flex/showroom property in Overland, MO. The five-year loan includes three years of interest-only payments and future funding. The borrower plans to stabilize the property and increase rents to market rates as existing leases expire.

data_points.project_notes: The five-year loan features three years of interest-only payments along with future funding.

articles.title: IRG, PREP Funds to Renovate 160,000 SF Industrial Property in Dayton, Ohio
articles.narrative: Industrial Realty Group LLC (IRG) and PREP Funds have acquired an industrial property at 5870 Poe Ave. in Dayton, Ohio, with plans to redevelop it into the Dayton Commerce Center. The 160,000-square-foot asset includes a main building with office space, multiple docks and drive-in doors, and heavy crane infrastructure, along with a smaller standalone building. Construction upgrades are set to begin immediately, and the ownership is actively seeking tenants for the repositioned space.

data_points.notable_features: Main building features 40,000 square feet of office space, six docks, four drive-in doors, and heavy crane infrastructure. Both structures offer 18-foot clear heights.

articles.title: Lee & Associates Negotiates Two Industrial Leases Totaling 131,417 SF in Chicago’s Western Suburbs
articles.narrative: Lee & Associates of Illinois has brokered two industrial leases in Chicago's western suburbs, totaling 131,417 square feet. Nuvomed Inc. leased 54,087 square feet in Hillside, with Clear Height Properties as the landlord. Separately, Recyclops Inc. secured 77,330 square feet in Forest Park, where ML Realty Partners is the landlord.

articles.title: Bernard Financial Group Arranges $7M Loan for Refinancing of Ohio Multifamily Property
articles.narrative: Bernard Financial Group has secured a $7 million permanent loan for the refinancing of a 250-unit multifamily property in Kettering, an inner suburb of Dayton. The loan was arranged through a life insurance company on behalf of the borrower, Fox Hunt Owner LLC.

articles.title: Gantry provides $32.5 million loan for multifamily community in Kansas City
articles.narrative: Gantry has secured a $32.5 million permanent loan for Edison at Tiffany Springs, a Class A multifamily community in Kansas City, MO. The financing serves as construction takeout for the 243-unit property, which was delivered in 2022. The 10-year, fixed-rate, non-recourse loan was provided through Freddie Mac, featuring partial interest-only payments before transitioning to a 35-year amortization schedule.

data_points.address: 7441 NW Old Tiffany Springs Rd, Kansas City, MO
data_points.notable_features: Class-A community with a clubhouse, resort-style pool, pickleball court, golf simulator, and in-unit finishes including nine-foot ceilings, stainless steel appliances, and granite countertops.
data_points.project_notes: Construction takeout financing for a property delivered in 2022.

articles.title: Ambrose completes pair of leases at industrial properties in Cincinnati, Denver
articles.narrative: Ambrose has completed two industrial leases totaling over 143,000 square feet across properties in Cincinnati and Denver. In Cincinnati, a material handling company leased 110,457 square feet at Cincinnati Logistics Park – Airport West, a four-building industrial development. In Denver, a third-party logistics provider secured 43,350 square feet at Ascent Commerce Center, marking its entry into the Colorado market and bringing Building I of that park to full occupancy. Both properties offer strategic access to major transportation infrastructure.

articles.title: Renewed growth in apartment rents … but not everywhere
articles.narrative: National apartment rents are showing signs of renewed growth, with median asking rents for U.S. one-bedroom apartments rising 0.5% in June from May to $1,526 a month, and two-bedroom rents increasing 0.1% to $1,905 monthly. This marks the first annual increase in one-bedroom rents in over a year, up 0.4% from June of last year, indicating a stabilization after a period of softening. The report highlights that supply remains the primary driver of rent performance, with markets delivering new units experiencing softer rents, while those with limited inventory see stronger growth. San Francisco exemplifies this trend with record-high rents and leading annual growth, contrasting with markets in Arizona that continue to report annual declines due to new supply.

articles.title: The Barry Company marketing 155,000-square-foot landmark office/industrial property in Menomonee
articles.narrative: The Barry Company has been selected to market a 155,000-square-foot office and industrial property in Menomonee Valley, Wisconsin, following the previous occupant's relocation to a larger headquarters. The landmark facility offers a combination of Class-A office space and high-clearance warehouse/production areas, with features suitable for single or multi-tenant occupancy.

data_points.notable_features: Features 32,000 SF of Class-A office space and 125,000 SF of warehouse/production space with 30-foot clear heights, abundant natural light, and potential for expansion or division. Located 15 minutes from Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport.

articles.title: Momentum, hope and positivity: They were on the menu at Cleveland Commercial Real Estate Summit
articles.narrative: The 12th annual Cleveland Commercial Real Estate Summit, hosted by Midwest Real Estate News and Northeast Ohio Properties magazines, conveyed an optimistic outlook for the Cleveland commercial real estate market. Panelists highlighted strong momentum in the healthcare, retail, and multifamily sectors, alongside the enduring resilience of the industrial market. While the office sector faces national challenges, positive signs are emerging, particularly in leasing activity for high-quality Class-A properties. The overall sentiment was that better times are ahead for Cleveland's commercial real estate.

articles.title: Barry Sternlicht raises $10B for fund eyeing data center push
articles.narrative: Starwood Capital Group has successfully raised $10.2 billion for its latest opportunistic commercial property fund, marking the largest such fund in the firm's history. Over a third of this capital is earmarked for data center investments, significantly increasing its allocation to the sector compared to previous funds. The fund, which secured commitments from over 300 investors, including a substantial contribution from Starwood itself, has already committed more than $3 billion across 20 investments, including a stake in a data center company, residential development land in Texas, and industrial assets in Northern Italy. Starwood plans to mitigate financing risk by seeking co-investors and extending development capital deployment over a longer timeframe, focusing on emerging rent growth markets in the Sun Belt for its rental housing investments.

articles.title: States defeat Trump administration in HUD homelessness funds case
articles.narrative: A U.S. District Judge ruled that the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) violated federal law by making changes to its Continuum of Care program, which provides billions in funding to states and municipalities for homelessness initiatives. The court found that HUD's policy changes, which would have shifted funding from permanent housing to temporary housing with work requirements and imposed a cap on permanent housing support, demonstrated "unreasoned decision making" and failed to consider the harm caused. This ruling allows a coalition of 20 states, led by New York, to continue receiving funds under the program's previous structure, which largely supported permanent housing.

articles.title: RLTYco acquires Atlanta-based commission advance company
articles.narrative: RLTYco, a provider of agent services, has acquired RealCommissions, an Atlanta-based commission advance company. This acquisition aims to expand RLTYco's commission advance offerings and address the fragmented nature of the industry. RealCommissions will maintain its brand and staff, with its founder continuing as a strategic advisor, as RLTYco seeks to professionalize the sector with lower fees and improved user experience.

articles.title: Trump raked in billions last year, including real estate riches
articles.narrative: Donald Trump's financial disclosures reveal he earned at least $2.2 billion last year, a significant increase from $622 million in 2024, primarily driven by cryptocurrency ventures. While crypto was the largest revenue source, real estate continues to be a substantial part of his fortune, generating over $35 million from Middle Eastern licensing deals and an additional $20 million from agreements in Vietnam, Romania, Turkey, Indonesia, and India. His U.S. properties, including golf clubs and Mar-a-Lago, contributed over $122 million and $77 million in revenue, respectively.

articles.title: NY Dirt: Mamdani touts largest transfer of assistance project
articles.narrative: The Mamdani administration has closed on the Sol on Park project, a $214 million affordable senior housing development in the Morrisania neighborhood of the Bronx. This project will create 229 affordable homes, with 80 units reserved for NYCHA residents and 68 units for formerly homeless seniors, making it the city's largest use of the "transfer of assistance" program. Developers NRP Group, Selfhelp Realty Group, and Foxy Management are targeting an early 2029 completion, demonstrating the administration's reliance on public-private partnerships to address the housing crisis.

data_points.notable_features: 80 units reserved for NYCHA residents, 68 units for formerly homeless seniors, and 80 units for low- and middle-income seniors. The project will include social services, a health and wellness center, and career training opportunities.
data_points.project_notes: The project is the city's largest use of its "transfer of assistance" program, which taps the federal Housing and Urban Development Department’s Rental Assistance Demonstration (RAD) program. It is being developed on the same site as the Morris Houses.

articles.market_intelligence: Developers have utilized a loophole in the city's 485x tax incentive program, resulting in 538 fewer affordable housing units than required. The program allows buildings with 99 units or fewer to reserve 20% of apartments for low- and middle-income tenants with a worker wage floor of $17/hour, while developments over 99 units require a 25% affordable housing minimum and a $63/hour worker wage floor. A federal appeals court has upheld New York's statewide mandate for all-electric buildings, banning gas hookups in new buildings under seven stories and applying to all sizes after January 1, 2029.

articles.title: NYC’s top deals: Soho penthouse trades for $10M
articles.narrative: ZAR Property NY has acquired a 12-story, 89,400-square-foot office building in New York City's Flatiron District for $28 million from GFP Real Estate. Additionally, two commercial properties in Jamaica, Queens, totaling 91,700 square feet of retail and office space, were sold for $17.3 million to 16101 Jamaica Avenue LLC by entities led by Leonard Zangas. These transactions highlight continued activity in the commercial real estate market across different boroughs of New York City.

data_points.address: 118 West 22nd Street, New York City, NY

articles.title: Policy Pro: NY electric buildings fight could reach the Supreme Court
articles.narrative: A recent ruling by the Second Circuit U.S. Court of Appeals has upheld New York state and city laws restricting fossil fuel appliances in new buildings, allowing the state's 2023 All-Electric Buildings Act and the city's 2021 Local Law 154 to proceed. This decision, however, creates a split among federal appeals courts, as the Ninth Circuit previously preempted a similar gas hookup ban in Berkeley, California. The plaintiffs, represented by Sarah Jorgensen, are considering an appeal, potentially setting the stage for the U.S. Supreme Court to resolve the conflicting interpretations of federal law. The outcome of this legal challenge could significantly influence the pace of electrification in New York's development pipeline and have national implications for building electrification policies.
articles.market_intelligence: New York's power grid is experiencing significant strain due to extreme heat, with electricity demand expected to reach seasonal peaks in the low-30,000-megawatt range. This sustained high demand increases the risk of localized power outages.

articles.title: Jared Solomon wants out of Brooklyn detention center
articles.narrative: Jared Solomon, a convicted fraudster formerly with Vornado Realty Trust, is seeking release from the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, citing brutal conditions and inadequate medical care. However, the U.S. Attorney's Office opposes his release, arguing that Solomon has violated prison rules regarding phone use and is "unsupervisable." The judge has not yet ruled on the bail application.

articles.title: NYCHA paperwork failures spark eviction wave
articles.narrative: A significant administrative failure within the New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) has led to an eviction crisis for hundreds of tenants in privately managed public housing developments under its PACT program. NYCHA's inability to process annual income recertifications resulted in the mistaken termination of Section 8 subsidies, causing private managers to bill tenants for full market rents. This error has led to a surge in eviction proceedings, particularly in East New York, despite tenants having paid their subsidized rent portions.

articles.title: Moishe Mana buys more land in Miami’s Allapattah
articles.narrative: Moishe Mana has expanded his extensive land holdings in Miami's Allapattah neighborhood, acquiring a 2.5-acre assemblage for $21.8 million from Allapattah East LLC. The 17 parcels, located between Northwest 20th and 22nd streets, will initially be used for parking, though Mana has not yet finalized long-term development plans. The seller indicated that the sale to a developer with a plan to activate the properties made strategic sense, given their own focus is not primarily on Miami at this time.

articles.title: Ex-con lists $138M in luxury penthouses, including Miami trophy condo
articles.market: Miami, FL / New York City, NY
articles.narrative: A former attorney and investor is listing two luxury penthouses for sale, one in Miami and one in New York City, with a combined asking price of $138 million. The Miami unit, a three-story residence in the Apogee complex, is listed for $78 million, while the New York City penthouse in Tribeca's Sky Lofts is asking $59.5 million. The seller, William Duker, is divesting these properties as he organizes the next phase of his life.

articles.title: Mixed-use mania: Mapping mall redevelopments planned in South Florida
articles.narrative: South Florida is experiencing a wave of mixed-use redevelopments at several shopping malls across Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. These projects aim to transform traditional retail centers into vibrant districts by adding thousands of apartments, alongside new retail, restaurants, offices, hotels, and entertainment venues. This trend is driven by the region's strong housing demand and mall owners' efforts to revitalize properties that have faced declining foot traffic and department store closures. However, many of these ambitious plans have encountered significant hurdles, including political opposition and legal challenges, impacting their progress.
articles.market_intelligence: Miami International Mall's CMBS loan has been in special servicing since February 2024, with the property valued at $143 million in June 2025, a 60% decrease from its $391 million valuation over a decade prior. As of September, the mall was 85% occupied overall, while the collateral portion backing the loan was 75% occupied.

articles.title: CIM Group uses credit bid to take Goodtime Hotel for $100 in foreclosure auction
articles.narrative: CIM Group, through an affiliate, acquired the Goodtime Hotel in South Beach, Miami Beach, via a foreclosure auction with a credit bid of $100. This transaction follows a $204.7 million foreclosure judgment obtained by CIM Group against the hotel's owner, an entity tied to developers Eric Birnbaum and Michael Fascitelli. The hotel, which opened in 2021, faced financial distress and a default on a $164 million loan provided by CIM Group in 2021.

data_points.notable_features: Seven-story hotel that opened in 2021 with celebrity partners.
data_points.project_notes: The site was previously acquired for $36 million in 2015. CIM Group obtained a $204.7 million foreclosure judgment, which included principal, interest, default interest, late fees, and attorney fees. The $100 bid was a credit bid to reduce property transfer taxes.

articles.title: Historic downtown Miami courthouse heads to auction with development caveats
articles.narrative: The historic Miami-Dade County Courthouse, a nearly century-old vacant building in downtown Miami, is being auctioned off, presenting a significant redevelopment opportunity. The 28-story property, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, is valued at $43 million and is zoned for high-density residential development, allowing up to 500 units per acre. While the exterior must be preserved, the interior offers flexibility for conversion, with a hotel or residential redevelopment considered more likely than office space due to the building's historic architecture and modern tenant expectations. The county previously attempted to redevelop the property, with one proposal from GFO Investments for a hotel, office, and residential tower, and the firm is expected to bid again.

data_points.notable_features: Listed in the National Register of Historic Places; civic institution zoning with rapid transit zoning overlay allowing up to 500 residential units per gross acre and unlimited floor area ratio; exterior must be preserved with interior features subject to preservation categories.
data_points.project_notes: Previously cost $32 million in maintenance and repairs over seven years. Miami-Dade County relocated civil court operations to the new Osvaldo N. Soto Miami-Dade Justice Center across the street in November.

articles.title: Chicago landlords spooked by expanded tenants’ rights ordinance
articles.narrative: Chicago landlords are expressing significant concern over proposed updates to the city's Residential Landlord and Tenant Ordinance, known as the Protecting Renters Ordinance. These updates include 'just cause' eviction requirements, mandatory relocation assistance for certain non-renewals, and caps on various rental fees. Landlord groups argue that these regulations will worsen the existing housing supply shortage and contribute to rising rents, rather than addressing affordability. Proponents, including Mayor Brandon Johnson, contend that the ordinance is essential to protect rent-burdened residents from displacement and predatory practices in a market increasingly prioritizing profit.

articles.title: Zillow kicks off antitrust showdown against Chicago MLS and Compass
articles.narrative: Zillow is engaged in a federal antitrust showdown against Midwest Real Estate Data (MRED), a Chicago-based multiple listing service, and brokerage giant Compass. The dispute centers on MRED's decision to temporarily cut off Zillow's listing feed, which Zillow alleges was a collusive effort by MRED and Compass to restrict market access and harm consumers. Zillow's Listing Access Standards, which prohibit listings previously marketed on private networks from appearing on its platform, are at the heart of the conflict, with MRED arguing these standards violate its objective criteria for listing display. The preliminary injunction hearing is examining whether MRED and Compass are unfairly limiting competition by restricting Zillow's access to crucial listing data.

articles.title: Stripe set to more than double office space to 222K sf in River North high-rise
articles.narrative: Stripe, an online payments solutions company, is significantly expanding its Chicago presence by leasing over 222,000 square feet at 350 North Orleans Street in River North. This new lease more than doubles their previous footprint in the building and will be occupied in phases as the company adds new hires. The expansion provides a boost to the property, which has faced challenges including a loan default by its previous owner.

data_points.project_notes: Stripe's new lease more than doubles its previous 89,000 square feet in the building. The property's previous owner, Blackstone, defaulted on a $310 million loan.

articles.market_intelligence: The office building at 350 North Orleans Street was just under 60 percent occupied last week. Bids for the building are in the $90 million to $100 million range, substantially less than the $378 million Blackstone paid in 2015. Another nearby property at 500 West Monroe Street sold for a 76 percent discount from its previous sale price.

articles.title: Revamped Mettawa mansion listed for just under $9M, second highest in Lake County
articles.narrative: A recently renovated 11,000-square-foot mansion in Mettawa, Illinois, known as Shagbark, has been listed for just under $9 million, making it the second-highest asking price in Lake County. The 1938-built property sits on 11 acres, featuring extensive amenities and designer furnishings. The owners undertook a substantial renovation, transforming several areas of the home and grounds.

data_points.notable_features: Features a 600-gallon saltwater aquarium, half basketball court, resort-style pool, cigar room, and comes fully furnished with designer furniture. The property includes 3.5 acres of irrigated grounds and 7.5 acres of tax-incentivized native prairie.
data_points.project_notes: The owners completed a substantial renovation, converting a library into a kitchen/social space, an outdoor potting shed into a cigar room, and an old kennel area into a gym, greenhouse, and animal pen.

articles.title: Oak Brook home lists for record price shy of $7M
articles.narrative: A luxury home in Oak Brook, IL, has been listed for nearly $7 million, setting a new record for the western Chicago suburb's residential listings. The property, located in the Ginger Creek community, spans 12,221 square feet on almost an acre of land. The listing price significantly exceeds the village's recent record sale of $5.3 million in October, highlighting the ambitious pricing in an unpredictable luxury housing market.

data_points.notable_features: Located in the Ginger Creek community, adjacent to Butterfield Country Club, with five bedrooms and 10 bathrooms.
data_points.project_notes: The property was last sold in 2011 for $4.25 million to 50 Baybrook Lane LLC.

articles.market_intelligence: The Oak Brook luxury home market has seen few successful sales above $5 million since 2003, with a recent $6.7 million listing from December remaining unsold. The highest recorded home sale in Oak Brook was $7.95 million in 2003. Recent luxury sales include a 10,000-square-foot mansion for $5.3 million in October, an 11,000-square-foot mansion for $4 million in December 2024, and a 12,000-square-foot property for $4.8 million in 2023.

articles.title: San Antonio broker and coffee shop owner indicted for identity theft and bank fraud
articles.narrative: A San Antonio real estate broker and coffee shop owner has been indicted on charges of bank fraud and identity theft. The charges stem from allegations that he misled a company into loaning him $2.12 million for an office property purchase in Grand Prairie, falsely claiming a key tenant had renewed its lease. This indictment is the latest in a series of legal challenges for the broker, including multiple default judgments in other real estate deals and the foreclosure sale of his coffee shop's flagship location.

data_points.project_notes: The loan was for the purchase of an office property. The borrower allegedly misrepresented that the Texas Facilities Commission had renewed its lease in the building.

articles.title: Klyde Warren Park expansion set to bring $4B in real estate value to Dallas
articles.narrative: The planned 1.7-acre expansion of Klyde Warren Park in Dallas is projected to generate approximately $3.5 billion in new real estate value through investment and tourism. The expansion, which includes a new green space called Jacobs Lawn and a two-story, 24,000-square-foot event and retail building, aims to further enhance the area's economic vitality. This initiative builds on the park's existing impact, which has already contributed an estimated $5.9 billion in real estate value to the Arts District and Uptown, resulting in significant incremental tax revenue for the city and county.

data_points.notable_features: Expansion includes Jacobs Lawn, a 37,000-square-foot green space that will convert to an ice skating rink in winter, and a two-story event and reception space with ground-floor retail.
data_points.project_notes: The park expansion is expected to generate $3.5 billion in new real estate value and has already contributed $5.9 billion in value to the Arts District and Uptown, yielding $957 million in incremental tax revenue.

articles.title: Greg Abbott calls for ban on new data centers in rural Texas communities
articles.narrative: Texas Governor Greg Abbott has proposed a ban on new data center developments in rural areas of the state, citing concerns over their impact on local communities and the state's power grid. This stance marks a shift from his previous support for AI infrastructure investment in Texas. The governor is also advocating for new regulations that would require data centers to contribute to the ERCOT-managed power grid, implement closed-loop water systems, and eliminate certain development incentives. This move comes as several Texas counties have unsuccessfully attempted local bans, and the city of San Marcos is currently testing the legality of the first city-level ban.

articles.title: Texas developers thought a state law to expand as-of-right housing production in commercial zones would help them build
articles.narrative: A new Texas state law, Senate Bill 840, intended to streamline housing development by allowing mixed-use and multifamily projects in commercial zones, is facing significant pushback and bureaucratic hurdles from local municipalities. Developers report that despite the law's intent to expand as-of-right housing, cities are employing various tactics, including new ordinances, rezoning, and informal stalling, to counteract its provisions. This creates a complex environment where developers must engage in extensive negotiation and politicking to advance projects, rather than benefiting from the intended deregulation. The situation highlights an ongoing power struggle between the state legislature's deregulation efforts and local governments' desire to maintain control over land use and development.

articles.title: Kelly Slater’s Austin Surf Club faces $16M in liens as it looks to restart construction
articles.narrative: The Austin Surf Club, a private artificial surf park and condo project, is facing over $16 million in construction liens, leading to a halt in work. The development, backed by notable figures in surfing and real estate, is seeking to establish a Municipal Management District to generate property tax revenue and fund infrastructure improvements. The project, planned for 178 private residences and a large surf basin, is located on the former NLand Surf Park site.

data_points.notable_features: Features a 2,200-foot-long surf basin and is marketed as a mixed-use lifestyle residential community.
data_points.project_notes: Construction paused in April 2026 due to over $16 million in construction liens. The project is being developed on the former site of NLand Surf Park, which closed in 2018. Developers are seeking to establish a Municipal Management District to fund infrastructure and remove the development from Austin's extra-territorial jurisdiction.

articles.title: Mission District apartment project moving forward after height, unit count reduction
articles.narrative: Wong Logan Architects is moving forward with a revised plan for Trigona, a six-story, 20-unit multifamily infill project in San Francisco's Mission District. The updated proposal reduces the building's height and nearly halves its residential capacity compared to previous plans, now including two deed-restricted affordable housing units. The project will also feature ground-floor commercial space and bicycle parking, situated on a triangular parcel one block from the 24th Street BART Station.

data_points.notable_features: Six-story building with 1,200 square feet of commercial space and parking for 18 bicycles, located one block from the 24th Street BART Station.
data_points.project_notes: The project includes two deed-restricted affordable housing units for low-income households. This is a revised plan, reduced from an earlier proposal that was two floors taller and had nearly double the residential capacity.

articles.market_intelligence: More than 20,000 housing units in San Francisco have been approved but are stalled in the development pipeline due to rising construction costs, city fees, material shortages, and federal tariffs. The City of San Francisco is mandated by the state to entitle 82,069 new housing units by 2030.

articles.title: Prologis scoops up vacant industrial site in San Jose
articles.narrative: Prologis has acquired a 14.2-acre vacant industrial site at 455 Piercy Road in San Jose for $14 million. The property was previously slated for a light industrial development by the former owner, InSite Property Group, but those plans appear to be abandoned. This acquisition further solidifies Prologis's position as a dominant industrial property owner in Silicon Valley.

data_points.project_notes: The 14.2-acre site was previously acquired in 2021 for nearly $4.8 million. Former owner InSite Property Group had proposed a 116,580-square-foot warehouse with 5,000 square feet of office space, but the development permit is set to expire by the end of 2026.

articles.market_intelligence: The south San Jose area has nearly 24 million square feet of industrial space.

articles.title: SF leads nation in trimming office vacancy rate as AI drives demand: CBRE
articles.narrative: San Francisco's office market is experiencing a significant recovery, primarily driven by the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence companies. The city recorded the largest year-over-year decline in office vacancy among major U.S. cities, falling to 29.7% in Q2 from 34.7% a year prior. AI firms have accounted for 30% of all leasing activity since 2023 and over three-quarters of net absorption, leading to a surge in market fundamentals, including increased asking rents and a record amount of tenant demand.
articles.market_intelligence: San Francisco's office vacancy rate fell by 5 percentage points year-over-year to 29.7% in Q2, the largest improvement nationally. AI companies are driving this recovery, accounting for 30% of leasing activity since 2023 and over 75% of net absorption. Asking rents increased 4.3% year-over-year to $71.67 per square foot. Tenants are currently seeking a record 8.9 million square feet of office space, with 3.1 million square feet from 53 AI companies.

articles.title: Before the IPO spree: Bay Area residential rankings
articles.narrative: The Bay Area's luxury residential market is experiencing an unprecedented boom, driven by the artificial intelligence industry's rapid growth and anticipated IPOs. Brokers report a surge in demand, dwindling supply, and escalating prices, with multiple multimillion-dollar offers becoming common. This trend is creating significant wealth for top real estate agents and brokerages in the region, with many expecting even higher peaks as major AI companies prepare to go public.

articles.title: Alexandria plots life sciences-to-housing pivot in Seattle’s Lower Queen Anne
articles.narrative: Alexandria Real Estate Equities is planning to redevelop a bioscience property in Seattle's Lower Queen Anne neighborhood into a 254-unit apartment building. The proposed eight-story project will span 274,500 square feet, with 174,000 square feet dedicated to residential space. Concurrently, Alexandria is marketing the 1.3-acre site for sale, aligning with its strategy to divest assets and diversify beyond life sciences real estate.

data_points.notable_features: Proposed eight-story building with 165 parking spaces.
data_points.project_notes: The 1.3-acre site was previously acquired in 2004 for $5.5 million. The existing property includes a 34,400-square-foot lab and office space. City Council approval for an alley vacation is expected in Q1 next year.

articles.title: Retail, Multifamily CMBS Delinquencies Rise in June as Overall Rate Moves Lower
articles.narrative: The Trepp CMBS Delinquency Rate saw a 20 basis point decrease in June 2026, settling at 7.35%, primarily due to a significant lodging loan cure. Despite this overall improvement, delinquency rates for retail and multifamily properties increased, with retail rising 30 basis points to 6.91% and multifamily increasing 28 basis points to 7.23%. Office delinquencies also saw a slight uptick, while lodging and industrial sectors experienced declines.

articles.title: Slatt Capital Arranges Acquisition Financing for Home2 Suites in Arkansas
articles.narrative: Slatt Capital successfully arranged a $9.49 million acquisition loan for the Home2 Suites, a 90-room hospitality property in Fort Smith, Arkansas. The financing, provided by Chambers Bank, features a three-year term with a 25-year amortization schedule and an 18-month interest-only period. The transaction highlights the property's strong performance, brand affiliation, and strategic location within the Fort Smith market, enabling the buyer to acquire this stabilized asset.

articles.title: Charney Acquires 143 Roebling in Williamsburg
articles.narrative: Charney Companies has acquired 143 Roebling St., a 100,000-square-foot mixed-use building in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, for $20 million. The company plans to restore and modernize the vacant property, which was originally built in 1907 and previously housed residential and retail spaces. Financing for the acquisition was provided by BH3 Fund Advisors.

data_points.notable_features: Historic building originally built in 1907, previously housed residential and retail spaces.

articles.title: Law Firms Load Up On Office Space To Handle AI Surge, Regulatory Chaos
articles.narrative: Law firms nationwide are significantly expanding their office footprints, reversing a decade-long trend of downsizing. This surge in demand for office space is driven by an explosion in caseloads related to increased artificial intelligence usage, rising regulatory uncertainty, and a more litigious business climate. Firms are signing larger leases, renewing early, and establishing satellite offices in growing markets to compete for specialized legal talent and accommodate new collaboration areas, war rooms, and high-end amenities. The legal sector's office growth reflects its recession-proof nature and consistent office-centricity, with firms strategically investing in placemaking and technology support staff.

articles.title: South Korean Culture Is Inspiring The Next Wave Of Apartment Amenities
articles.narrative: South Korean cultural influences, particularly in longevity-focused wellness, are increasingly shaping amenity design in U.S. apartment buildings. Developers are moving beyond traditional gyms and party rooms to incorporate holistic wellness features like hot-cold plunge pools, Himalayan salt rooms, and sensory showers, drawing inspiration from East Asian spa traditions. This shift reflects a growing demand among renters for amenities that support mind-body connection, stress relief, and recovery, with developers betting on residents' willingness to pay for services that promote a longer, healthier life.

articles.title: 'We Dodged A Bullet': Mass. Multifamily Market Starts To Thaw After Rent Control Ruling
articles.narrative: Following a Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court ruling that blocked a statewide rent control ballot measure, the multifamily investment market in Massachusetts is showing signs of recovery. Industry experts and brokers report an immediate uptick in deal conversations, signed contracts, and renewed investor confidence, which had been significantly dampened by the prospect of the restrictive policy. While the ruling has thawed the market, participants are proceeding with cautious optimism, acknowledging that rent control advocates are likely to reintroduce a revised measure in the future. The initial proposal would have capped rent increases at 5% or the CPI, whichever was lower, and its potential passage had led to a substantial decline in multifamily sales volume across the state.

articles.title: Best First Half For NYC Offices Since 2002 Puts Landlords Back In Control
articles.narrative: New York City's office market experienced its strongest first half for leasing activity since 2002, with 22.8 million square feet leased through June, putting it on track for the busiest year since 2000. This surge in demand, driven by law firms and AI companies, combined with a reduction in available supply due to office-to-residential conversions, has significantly tightened the market. As a result, the citywide availability rate dropped to 13%, the lowest since October 2020, and average asking rents increased by 5.7% year-over-year to $78.03 per square foot, indicating a shift in leverage back to landlords.
articles.market_intelligence: The New York City office market is experiencing a significant tightening, with availability rates at their lowest since October 2020. This is driven by strong leasing activity, particularly from law firms and AI companies, and a reduction in supply due to office-to-residential conversions. The conversions not only reduce available space but also generate additional demand as displaced tenants seek new offices. Average asking rents have seen their sharpest midyear growth since 2016, and the spread between taking rents and asking rents is narrowing, indicating a shift in market power towards landlords.
